name: KY-04
label: Safe R

Prediction markets price a Republican win at ~96%

model.rationale: Kentucky's 4th District carries an R+18 lean and prediction markets give the Republican nominee roughly a 96% win probability, while the Democratic nominee has raised under $100,000 with no outside spending. The open seat adds some uncertainty, but nothing suggests a competitive general election.
model.watch: A serious polling error or unexpected Democratic outside spending could move this toward Lean R, but no such evidence exists.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is an open seat after Republican Thomas Massie lost renomination, but the seat itself remains deeply Republican territory with an R+18 partisan lean. Ed Gallrein enters the general election with strong fundraising and heavy outside spending on both sides of the primary aftermath, while Democrat Melissa Strange has raised under $100,000 and drawn no outside support. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is minimally funded.

Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican hold in the mid-to-high teens.
